scope: Focused primary-source mathematical/model comparison. Negative searches do not certify novelty.
overall: F132 and its all-length extension are supported proof-level syntheses of established tabulation and stable Fourier interpolation mechanisms. No inspected primary source literally establishes the entire same finite-word/cold/all-input relative-l2 contract; worldwide novelty remains unresolved.

comparisons.title: Faster Walsh-Hadamard Transform and Matrix Multiplication over Finite Fields using Lookup Tables
comparisons.inspected: Sections 1, 3 and 5; Lemma 3.1, Theorem 3.2, word-RAM permutation discussion
comparisons.finding: Exact constant-field Kronecker transforms already attain the logarithmic saving by fully enumerated small-block tables. Section 5 separately discusses packed word-RAM permutation costs. F132 uses the same established mechanism, with rounded complex states, normwise stability, and O(r) paid gathering/output for each r-coordinate block.
comparisons.disposition: Mechanism precedent established; not a literal complex relative-l2 theorem or priority clearance.

comparisons.title: Matrix-Vector Multiplication in Sub-Quadratic Time (Some Preprocessing Required)
comparisons.inspected: Theorems 1.1–1.2 and discussion of block lookup preprocessing
comparisons.finding: Finite-semiring matrix-vector multiplication with preprocessing is an established general tabulation setting. Its superquadratic preprocessing and dense-matrix query problem do not supply F132’s cold, near-linear Fourier setup or numerical error contract. Calling the finite-alphabet table principle itself new would be incorrect.
comparisons.disposition: General finite-state/tabulation precedent established; model-specific F132 corollary still needs its proof.

comparisons.title: SWIFFT: A Modest Proposal for FFT Hashing
comparisons.inspected: Section 3, binary-input lookup tables for initial FFT iterations
comparisons.finding: The paper explicitly tabulates initial finite-field FFT levels on binary inputs. This is a direct FFT implementation precedent, not only a matrix-multiplication analogy. It does not assert the cold all-input rounded-complex norm theorem, repeated re-quantization, or its growing accuracy/radix schedule.
comparisons.disposition: FFT-specific lookup reuse is established prior art.

comparisons.title: How Fast Can We Multiply Large Integers on an Actual Computer?
comparisons.inspected: Log-RAM model and Section 4.1/Theorem 1 integer multiplication comparison
comparisons.finding: The O(n) log-RAM integer-multiplication result partitions n input bits into roughly n/log n complex coefficients. N independently represented Fourier coefficients may contain Theta(N log N) bits. Substituting that aggregate input size does not directly imply an O(N log N/log log N) N-coordinate DFT.
comparisons.disposition: Relevant word-cost precedent; previously alleged direct subsumption is not justified.

comparisons.authors: Chan, Jin, Vassilevska Williams and Xu
comparisons.title: Faster Algorithms for Text-to-Pattern Hamming Distances
comparisons.inspected: Lemma 2.2 and Appendix B model, statement and proof architecture
comparisons.finding: Lemma 2.2 gives deterministic O(n log p) word-RAM convolution over F_p; Appendix B repairs an earlier packed-convolution argument and uses bit tricks and tables. Exact modular convolution is not a complex DFT with relative-l2 accuracy. This strengthens the required finite-field packing comparison without proving subsumption.
comparisons.disposition: Important modern comparator; model and target differ.

comparisons.title: Fast Fourier Transforms for Nonequispaced Data
comparisons.inspected: Primary publisher abstract, scope, complexity and bibliography
comparisons.finding: Oversampled/analytic Fourier interpolation with O(N log N+N log(1/epsilon)) arithmetic work is classical. The new all-length result composes that established idea with F132 and proves its specific separated-grid operator norm, finite-state coefficient tables and cold word costs. The interpolation principle is not claimed new.
comparisons.disposition: Classical all-length compiler mechanism; exact new composition proved locally.

comparisons.title: Numerical Stability of Fast Trigonometric Transforms: A Worst Case Study
comparisons.inspected: Sections 2–3, twiddle precomputation and normwise stability Theorems 3.3/3.6
comparisons.finding: Normwise FFT stability through sparse unitary factorizations and careful twiddle preparation is established. The paper explicitly distinguishes stable generation from recurrences whose errors grow with length. F132’s accuracy guarantee should be credited as an application of this tradition, with additional finite-alphabet and paid-table accounting.
comparisons.disposition: Stability mechanism classical; no tabulated sub-N-log-N theorem claimed by this source.

comparisons.title: Numerical Stability of Nonequispaced Fast Fourier Transforms
comparisons.inspected: Algorithm 2.1, equations (2.5)/(2.6), sampling separation and stability discussion
comparisons.finding: The paper explicitly uses dyadic oversampling, localized windows and truncated evaluation. Its displayed generic Euclidean bounds include dimension-dependent factors; they cannot simply be substituted as a dimension-free epsilon contract. Our separated-grid Schur argument supplies the needed bound for this special all-length compiler.
comparisons.disposition: Close primary comparator; avoids importing a looser error norm.

comparisons.title: Uniform error estimates for nonequispaced fast Fourier transforms
comparisons.inspected: Primary abstract, window-family framework and uniform-error scope
comparisons.finding: Uniform NFFT window-error analysis has an extensive existing literature. A new fast Fourier claim must distinguish interpolation error, arithmetic error, relative energy accuracy and word complexity. This source reinforces that the window approximation itself is an established research area, rather than evidence of priority for the proposed composition.
comparisons.disposition: Background comparator; no complete theorem-matched subsumption asserted.

comparisons.title: Bluestein Design Document
comparisons.inspected: Chirp definition, convolution embedding and FFT reduction
comparisons.finding: Bluestein’s chirp-convolution reduction is standard. The new negative derivation concerns applying an l2-only approximate FFT contract to its kernel spectrum: an allowed error can amplify by Theta(sqrt N). It is not a claim that the classical identity is incorrect or that all implementations suffer that error.
comparisons.disposition: Identity classical; black-box precision obstruction derived independently.
